title: The login page is real; the app is not
scenario: A link opens a genuine Microsoft/Google login page. After signing in, a third-party app asks for permission to read your mail, files, contacts and calendar “to deliver the document.”

answers.A: Review the publisher and exact permissions with security before granting anything.
answers.B: Approve because the login page is genuine and the provider would block malicious apps.
answers.C: Do not approve; close it and access the document through the company’s approved collaboration tools or verify the app with IT.

explanation: OAuth abuse can use a real login page and still grant a malicious app persistent access.
proTip: Authenticate the app, not just the login page.
